main_topics.reason: The user repeatedly asked which RA medications fit with trying to conceive and pregnancy, and how to plan the transition over the next one to two years.
After learning methotrexate needs to be stopped before conception, the user said they had just started it and asked whether to worry, then discussed contraception and washout timing.
The user asked what would happen if a pregnancy-compatible regimen did not control their RA as well as methotrexate.
The user asked whether RA symptoms can change during pregnancy and noted wanting to prepare for postpartum flares.
The user asked whether pregnancy-compatible medications are also compatible with breastfeeding.
The user asked who should be involved and whether to raise pregnancy plans with the rheumatologist now.
The user described being scared they might have to choose between their health and having a baby, and later said they felt less anxious.

output.summary: The user, recently diagnosed with RA and taking methotrexate, wanted to plan for trying for a baby in one to two years. The assistant discussed medication options and timing, disease control, pregnancy and postpartum changes, breastfeeding, and care-team coordination; the user said the recap was exactly right and that they felt they had a handle on the plan.
